General

- The NMDA receptor is made of 4 membrane spanning subunits and is a voltage sensitive  ligand gated ion channel. 
- Its primary ligand is glutamate with glycine as a co-agonist binding at non glutamate binding site 

Activation process:

- Priming of membrane by AMPA brings RMP → partial depolarisation 
- Mg2+ displaced from NMDA receptor pore 
- Binding of glutamate and glycine 
- Ion flux: influx of Ca2+ and Na+, efflux of K+

Ketamine antagonism:

- Ketamine is a NMDA receptor non-competitive antagonist binding at an allosteric site producing analgesia and a dissociative hypnotic state 
- Prevents ion flux → prevents neuronal depolarisation 
- Downstream effect depends on cell type includes:

> ↓Ca^2+^-mediated cell activation
>
> ↓2^nd^ messenger signalling
>
> ↓Gene transcription
